examples.en: A scandal about the celebrity came out in the news.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 추문 때문에 자리에서 물러났어요.
examples.en: That politician stepped down because of a scandal.
The company was caught up in a scandal, and its stock price fell.
I heard they lied to cover up the scandal.
Rumors and scandals spread fast.
The singer whose image suffered from a scandal made a comeback.

explain: 도덕적으로 좋지 않은 일이 소문이나 기사로 알려진 것을 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '스캔들'이라고 많이 하고, '추문'은 기사나 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: That singer was caught up in a scandal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기사에서 가장 자주 보이는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common expression in news.

phrases.en: A strange scandal spread around the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소문처럼 퍼진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it spreads like a rumor.

phrases.en: That actor's scandal is the talk of the town.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '스캔들'이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in everyday talk.

explain_en: Scandal that damages reputation; written, sometimes false claims. It means a morally embarrassing matter that has become known through rumor or news. In everyday talk people often say '스캔들', while '추문' shows up more in articles and writing.

en: to encroach on; to invade; to violate

examples.en: The neighboring country's army crossed the border.
You must not invade other people's privacy.

examples.ko: 동생이 제 방을 침범해서 화가 났어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling barged into my room, and I got angry.

examples.ko: 새로 온 사람이 제 자리를 침범하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It feels like the newcomer is encroaching on my spot.
Do not infringe on other people's rights.
I demanded an apology from the person who had intruded.

explain: '침입하다'는 건물이나 장소에 몰래 들어가는 쪽이고, '침범하다'는 땅·권리·사생활 같은 남의 영역을 넘어오는 쪽이에요. 도둑은 '침입'하고, 영해와 사생활은 '침범'해요.

phrases.en: Our country's airspace was violated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 침범을 당한 쪽에서 말하는 표현이에요. 영공, 영해, 권리와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side that was encroached upon. Fits airspace, waters, and rights.

phrases.en: Please don't intrude on other people's territory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅뿐 아니라 일이나 공간처럼 남의 몫을 넘어올 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for land, but also for someone's work or space when you cross into it.

phrases.example: 다른 사람의 권리를 침해하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not infringe on other people's rights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권리나 이익을 해칠 때 써요. '침범'은 경계를 넘어 들어오는 느낌이고, '침해'는 권리를 해치는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when harming rights or interests. 침범 feels like crossing a boundary, while 침해 feels like damaging a right.

explain_en: Cross into others' territory or boundaries, physical or abstract. '침입하다' is about sneaking into a building or place, while '침범하다' is about crossing into someone else's territory, rights, or privacy. A thief '침입하다', but territorial waters and privacy are '침범하다'.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 상장 퇴출 위기에 놓였어요.
examples.en: That company is in danger of being delisted.
The player who broke the rules was kicked out of the tournament.

examples.ko: 안전 기준을 못 지킨 제품은 시장에서 퇴출돼요.
examples.en: Products that fail safety standards are pulled from the market.

examples.ko: 방송에서 논란이 된 출연자의 퇴출을 요구하는 글이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many posts demanding the removal of a controversial guest from the show.

examples.ko: 실적이 나쁜 가게는 퇴출 대상이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: A store with poor results can become a target for removal.

examples.ko: 퇴출 소식에 그 팀 팬들이 크게 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The team's fans were shocked at the news of the expulsion.

explain: 어떤 곳이나 자리에서 쫓겨나 나가게 될 때 써요. 회사의 상장, 시장, 방송, 대회처럼 공식적인 곳에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 학생이 학교에서 나가는 건 '퇴학', 직원이 회사에서 나가는 건 '해고'라고 해요.

phrases.en: That player was kicked out for breaking the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 퇴출의 동사 표현으로, 쫓겨나는 사람이나 회사 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, said from the view of whoever is being removed.

phrases.en: That shop is at risk of being forced out of the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 쫓겨날 수도 있는 어려운 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a difficult situation where removal may be coming.

phrases.en: The company pulled that product from the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 쫓아내거나 없애는 쪽 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the one who removes someone or something.

explain_en: Forced removal from a market or group; news, business. It is used when something or someone is forced out of a place or position. It is a stiff word for official settings like stock listings, markets, broadcasts, or tournaments. A student leaving school this way is 퇴학, and an employee is 해고.

t90.ax: That company is in danger of being delisted.

en: to be inclined; to tend; to be biased

examples.ko: 이 뉴스는 한쪽 입장으로 편향되어 있어요.
examples.en: This news report is biased toward one side.

examples.ko: 편향된 생각을 버리고 다시 판단해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's drop the biased thinking and judge again.

examples.ko: 설문 결과가 젊은 사람에게 편향돼 있어요.
examples.en: The survey results are skewed toward young people.
People easily become biased by their own experience.

examples.ko: 식사가 고기에 편향되면 건강에 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: If your meals lean too heavily on meat, it is not good for your health.
The article was so biased that it was hard to believe.

explain: 한쪽으로 치우쳐서 공정하지 않은 상태를 말해요. 뉴스, 시각, 생각, 자료와 자주 같이 써요. '치우치다'는 일상에서도 쓰지만 편향되다는 글이나 뉴스 느낌이 나요. 반대로 공평하고 균형 잡힌 것은 '공정하다', '균형이 잡히다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 편향된 시각으로 보면 사실이 잘 안 보여요.
phrases.en: If you look with a biased view, the facts are hard to see.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~ㄴ' 형태로 명사를 꾸며서 치우친 생각을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used to criticize a one-sided way of thinking.

phrases.example: 이 기사는 편향되지 않아서 믿을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This article isn't biased, so you can trust it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 공정하다는 뜻을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says something is fair and balanced.

phrases.en: His thinking leans to one side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 일상에서도 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar, easier expression that works in daily talk.

explain_en: Opinions or views lean unfairly to one side (편향된 생각) It describes leaning to one side in a way that is not fair. It often goes with news, viewpoints, thinking, and data. '치우치다' also works in daily talk, while 편향되다 sounds like writing or news. The opposite, being fair and balanced, is '공정하다' or '균형이 잡히다'.

t90.ax: This news report is biased toward one side.

examples.en: During the war, planes bombed the city.

examples.ko: 비행기가 다리를 폭격하는 장면이 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: A scene where a plane bombs a bridge appears in the movie.
There was a plan to bomb the enemy base.
The news reported the fact that the village had been bombed.
The planes carried out a bombing run, and the building collapsed.
They bombed first, and then the soldiers moved in.

explain: 비행기 같은 것으로 위에서 폭탄을 떨어뜨려 공격하는 것에 써요. '폭파하다'는 다리나 건물을 터뜨려 부수는 일이라서 달라요. 전쟁 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 도시는 전쟁 중에 폭격을 받았어요.
phrases.en: That city was bombed during the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: '폭격하다'의 반대쪽 입장에서 쓰는 표현으로, 공격을 당하는 쪽을 주어로 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The expression from the other side, with the attacked place as the subject.

phrases.en: A bomber flew across the sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 폭탄을 떨어뜨리는 비행기를 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for an aircraft that drops bombs.

phrases.en: That plane did not bomb the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 공격하지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used in news or history when saying something was not bombed.

explain_en: It is for attacking by dropping bombs from above, with aircraft for example. 폭파하다 is different: it means blowing up a bridge or building. It shows up often in war news and history.

examples.en: I am unhappy with the verdict, so I am preparing an appeal.

examples.ko: 항소는 판결이 나온 뒤 정해진 기간 안에 해야 해요.
examples.en: An appeal has to be filed within a set period after the ruling.
The lawyer explained the grounds for the appeal.

examples.ko: 항소가 받아들여져서 재판을 다시 하게 됐어요.
examples.en: The appeal was accepted, so the trial is being held again.
The company accepted the ruling without an appeal.
New evidence is important in this appeal.

explain: 1심 판결 뒤에 하는 것이 '항소'이고, 2심 뒤에 대법원에 하는 것은 '상고'예요. 보통 '항소를 하다', '항소를 제기하다'로 쓰고, 동사로는 '항소하다'를 써요. 뉴스와 법 이야기에서만 나와요.

phrases.en: The defendant disagreed with the verdict and filed an appeal.
phrases.nuance_ko: '항소를 하다'보다 법 뉴스에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more formal than 항소를 하다 and is common in legal news.

phrases.en: The result changed in the appeal trial.
phrases.nuance_ko: 항소 때문에 다시 열리는 재판을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the trial held again because of an appeal.

phrases.en: The prosecutor will appeal soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '항소'를 동사로 바꾼 말로 짧게 말할 때 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 항소, handy for saying it more briefly.

explain_en: Formal court term; challenging a verdict by appealing to a higher court. An appeal made after a first trial is 항소; one made to the Supreme Court after the second trial is 상고. It is used as '항소를 하다' or '항소를 제기하다', and the verb form is 항소하다. It appears only in news and legal talk.

en: to be in confusion; to be in chaos; to be in disorder

examples.en: The work changed suddenly, so my head is a mess.
Right after the accident, the scene was chaotic.
In chaotic times, act calmly.
The explanation is so complicated that I'm even more confused.

examples.ko: 마음이 혼란하면 일단 쉬는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: When your mind is in turmoil, it's best to rest first.
I'm so confused that I don't know where to start.

explain: 머릿속이 정리되지 않을 때도, 사회나 장소가 질서 없이 뒤죽박죽일 때도 써요. '혼란스럽다'는 그런 느낌이 든다는 말이라 사람 마음에 더 자주 쓰이고, '혼란하다'는 상황·시기·현장에 어울려요. '복잡하다'는 얽혀 있다는 뜻이라 질서가 무너졌다는 느낌은 없어요.

phrases.en: The time right after the war was a chaotic period.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼란한'으로 바꿔 시기나 상황을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier '혼란한' describes a period or situation.

phrases.en: There is so much information that I feel confused.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼란스럽다'는 그렇게 느낀다는 말이라 사람 마음에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '혼란스럽다' means feeling confused, so it suits a person's state of mind better.

phrases.en: The room is a total mess.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼란하다'와 비슷하게 순서 없이 엉망일 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word for when things are jumbled and out of order, like '혼란하다'.

explain_en: Covers both a muddled mind and a society or place without order. '혼란스럽다' is more about how you feel, while '혼란하다' fits situations, periods and scenes. '복잡하다' only means tangled, with no sense that order has collapsed.

examples.en: Fake news is rampant on the internet these days.
Scam texts are everywhere, so we have to be careful.
During exam season, false rumors tend to run wild.
We cleaned up the street where illegal ads were rampant.

examples.ko: 이런 나쁜 습관이 횡행하게 두면 안 돼요.
examples.en: We shouldn't let these bad habits run rampant.
They say cheating was rampant in the past.

explain: 소문, 사기, 부정행위 같은 나쁜 일이 거리낌 없이 널리 퍼질 때 써요. 좋은 일이나 중립적인 일에는 '유행하다'를 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: Delivery scams are rampant before the holidays.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일의 이름을 주어로 넣어 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern, with the bad thing as the subject.

phrases.example: 횡행하는 부정행위를 막기 위해 시험 규칙이 바뀌었어요.
phrases.en: The exam rules changed to stop rampant cheating.
phrases.nuance_ko: '횡행하는 + 명사' 형태로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The 횡행하는 + noun form modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.en: A false rumor spread widely through the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 중립적인 말이에요. '횡행하다'처럼 나쁜 일이라는 판단은 들어 있지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, neutral phrase without the negative judgment of 횡행하다.

explain_en: Use it when bad things such as rumors, scams or cheating spread widely without restraint. For good or neutral things, use '유행하다' instead. You often see it in news and writing.

examples.en: There is a good chance of rain tomorrow.

examples.ko: 이번 경기는 우리 팀이 이길 공산이 높아요.
examples.en: Our team is likely to win this game.

examples.ko: 그 계획이 성공할 공산은 크지 않아요.
examples.en: The chance that the plan succeeds is not high.

examples.ko: 값이 더 오를 공산이 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say prices could rise further.

examples.ko: 회의가 길어질 공산이 커서 점심을 미리 먹었어요.
examples.en: The meeting was likely to run long, so I ate lunch beforehand.

examples.ko: 늦게 출발하면 길이 막힐 공산이 많아요.
examples.en: If we leave late, the roads will probably be jammed.

explain: 공산은 '-ㄹ 공산이 크다/높다/많다/있다' 모양으로 써요. 앞일이 일어날 가능성을 말할 때 쓰고 '가능성'보다 뉴스나 글에서 딱딱하게 들려요. 같은 소리의 '공산당'과는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: There is a good chance of passing this exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공산이 높다'와 같은 뜻으로, 가능성이 크다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'high likelihood', saying a chance is large.

phrases.en: There is little chance of snow today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그렇게 될 가능성이 낮다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the chance of something happening is low.

phrases.example: 그 계획이 성공할 공산이 거의 없어요.
phrases.en: There is almost no chance that plan will succeed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가능성이 거의 없다는 강한 말이에요. '거의'를 붙이면 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong phrase saying there is almost no chance; adding 'almost' makes it sound more natural.

explain_en: Chance that something will happen, used in (공산이 크다) with forecasts. This word is used in the pattern '-ㄹ 공산이 크다/높다/많다/있다' (it is likely that...). It sounds stiffer than '가능성' and fits the news and writing. It is a different word from the 공산 in '공산당' (communist party).

examples.ko: 과학에 대한 맹신도 문제가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Blind faith in science can also be a problem.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 점에 대한 맹신이 심해요.
examples.en: He has a strong blind faith in fortune-telling.

examples.ko: 한 가지 의견만 믿는 맹신은 판단을 흐려요.
examples.en: Blind faith in just one opinion clouds your judgment.

examples.ko: 후기 맹신 때문에 실패한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once failed because I trusted reviews blindly.

examples.ko: 유명인의 말에 대한 맹신을 버려야 해요.
examples.en: We should give up our blind trust in celebrities' words.
I broke free from blind trust and checked it myself.

explain: 믿음이 깊다는 좋은 뜻이 아니라 따져 보지 않고 무조건 믿는다는 부정적인 느낌이에요. 반대로는 '의심하다', '비판적으로 보다' 같은 말을 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 점에 대한 맹신에 빠져 있어요.
phrases.en: He has fallen into blind faith in fortune-telling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 따져 보지 않고 믿는 상태가 되었다는 부정적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative phrase meaning one began to believe without questioning.

phrases.en: Blind faith in anything is dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조언이나 충고를 할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when giving advice or a warning.

phrases.example: 뉴스에 대한 무조건적인 맹신은 좋지 않아요.
phrases.en: Unconditional blind faith in the news is not good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무조건적인'을 붙이면 비판하는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '무조건적인' makes the criticism clearer.

explain_en: Believing something without doubt, negative nuance (광고를 맹신하다) It does not mean deep faith in a good sense; it is negative, implying believing without questioning. Its opposites are things like '의심하다' and '비판적으로 보다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 일이 많아서 심적 부담이 커요.
examples.en: I have so much work lately that the mental burden is heavy.

examples.ko: 그 사고 후에 심적으로 많이 힘들었어요.
examples.en: After that accident, I had a really hard time mentally.

examples.ko: 심적 안정을 위해 며칠 쉬기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to rest for a few days for my peace of mind.
Mental changes affect the body too.
I comforted my friend, who was mentally worn out.

examples.ko: 시험 전에는 심적 여유를 갖는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: It is important to keep some mental ease before an exam.

explain: '심적 부담', '심적 고통', '심적 안정'처럼 명사 앞에 오거나 '심적으로'의 형태로 써요. '육체적'의 반대 쪽인 '정신적'과 가깝지만, 말할 때는 그냥 '마음이 힘들다'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I suffered mental pain for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 아프고 괴로운 상태를 글이나 공식적인 말에서 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes emotional suffering in writing or formal speech.

phrases.en: After the trip, I found my peace of mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 편안하고 흔들리지 않는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a calm, steady state of mind.

phrases.en: I've been very worn out mentally lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심적'과 가까운 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자주 들리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 심적 and more common in speech.

explain_en: It appears before nouns, as in '심적 부담', '심적 고통' and '심적 안정', or in the form '심적으로'. It is close to '정신적' (the opposite of '육체적'), but in speech people often simply say '마음이 힘들다'.

en: to be bleak; to be grim; to be hopeless

examples.en: My future looks so bleak that I can't sleep.
There is a lot of news saying the job market looks bleak.

examples.ko: 갑자기 해고 통보를 받고 눈앞이 암담했어요.
examples.en: I was suddenly told I was fired, and everything looked hopeless.
After hearing the news, my heart sank into gloom.

examples.ko: 암담한 현실 속에서도 희망을 놓지 않았어요.
examples.en: I didn't let go of hope even in the bleak reality.
I have no money or job, so I feel completely hopeless.

explain: '막막하다'와 비슷하지만, '암담하다'는 어둡고 희망이 안 보이는 느낌이 더 커요. '앞날이', '현실이', '전망이'와 자주 같이 써요. 이야기할 때보다 글이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: I just sigh, worried about my bleak future.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사를 '-ㄴ'으로 바꿔 명사를 꾸미는 가장 흔한 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, turning the adjective into -ㄴ to modify a noun.

phrases.en: The current situation looks truly hopeless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 보기에 희망이 없어 보인다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it looks hopeless from the outside.

phrases.en: I have no idea what to do after graduation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 '막막하다'는 어떻게 할지 몰라 답답한 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but 막막하다 stresses feeling stuck with no idea what to do.

explain_en: Hopeless about the future or prospects (앞날이 암담하다) It is similar to '막막하다', but '암담하다' leans more toward darkness and no hope in sight. It often goes with '앞날이' (the future), '현실이' (reality) and '전망이' (outlook). It appears more in writing and the news than in casual talk.

t90.ax: My future looks so bleak that I can't sleep.

en: lightly; as if it were nothing special

examples.en: Don't take those words lightly.
My friend lies as if it were nothing, and I'm worried.
I don't let even a small mistake pass as no big deal.

examples.ko: 예사로 지나쳤던 일이 나중에 큰 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: Something I had brushed off became a big problem later.

examples.ko: 그는 약속을 어기는 걸 예사로 여겨요.
examples.en: He treats breaking promises as an ordinary thing.

examples.ko: 이 증상은 예사로 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't treat this symptom as nothing.

explain: '대수롭지 않게, 보통 일처럼'이라는 느낌으로 '예사로 넘기다, 예사로 보다, 예사로 여기다, 예사로 하다'처럼 뒤의 동사와 함께 써요. '예사롭지 않다'가 훨씬 자주 나오는 형태라서 같이 익혀 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: That person's gaze is not ordinary.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예사로'의 반대 느낌으로 가장 자주 나오는 형태이고, 심상치 않다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most frequent form, carrying the opposite feel of '예사로': out of the ordinary.

phrases.en: Don't brush off even small problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대수롭지 않게 그냥 지나친다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means passing over something as if it were nothing.

phrases.example: 그는 약속을 어기는 걸 예사로 여겨요.
phrases.en: He treats breaking promises as nothing special.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 일도 아무렇지 않게 생각하는 모습에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for taking even bad things lightly.

explain_en: It carries the feel of 'as if it were nothing special' and goes with verbs such as '예사로 넘기다, 예사로 보다, 예사로 여기다, 예사로 하다'. The negative form '예사롭지 않다' is much more common, so it is worth learning together.

examples.en: Dependence on smartphones is steadily increasing.

examples.ko: 의존성이 강한 아이는 혼자 결정하기 어려워해요.
examples.en: A child with strong dependency has trouble deciding alone.

examples.ko: 이 약은 의존성이 생길 수 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: This medicine can cause dependence, so you need to be careful.
Our country has a high reliance on imports.
To become an adult, you need to reduce dependence.
I received counseling because of my dependence on games.

explain: '의존'이 기대는 일 자체라면 '의존성'은 그런 성질이나 정도를 말해요. '높다/낮다, 강하다, 줄이다'와 함께 쓰고, 걱정스러운 문제를 이야기할 때 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 요즘 사람들은 스마트폰에 대한 의존성이 높아요.
phrases.en: These days people have a high dependence on smartphones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대는 정도가 클 때 쓰고, 반대는 '낮다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reliance is strong; the opposite is 낮다.

phrases.en: We must reduce our dependence on imported energy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제를 해결하려는 방향의 말을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about solving a dependence problem.

phrases.example: 우리 회사는 한 고객에 대한 의존도가 커요.
phrases.en: Our company relies heavily on one customer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의존성'과 비슷하지만 '얼마나 기대는지'의 정도를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 의존성 but focuses on the degree of reliance.

explain_en: While '의존' is the act of relying, '의존성' refers to that tendency or its degree. It goes with words like '높다/낮다', '강하다' and '줄이다', and often appears when talking about worrying problems.
